statement: GL-free admission plans inclusive day/night, 120-second weather and three-day schedules with exact ticks, rational bursts and final-tick holds under 4096-frame and 10-million-tick ceilings. The sequence execution protocol re-admits immutable plans and checks aggregate transport-provided frame/manifest byte reservations against a caller-lowered 512 GiB ceiling before executable steps. It requests and verifies individual simulation ticks, bounds frozen warmup/readiness/settling and presentation substeps, derives calendar phase from ticks and carries explicit lighting controls. Sticky refusal and a final publication acknowledgement prevent partial captures from becoming complete in the protocol. Registered regressions cover schedules, readiness, phase, budgets, clock/transport faults and real creature-brain progression matching ordinary fixed ticking. QA runtime admission now accepts a canonical fresh 30 Hz world at fixed spawn/full-frame, checks A4 staging and aggregate output reservations before startup writes, and drives simulation/physics exclusively from the plan. The world sweep shares this single runtime admission and sequence through a GL-free transport, resolved-clock checks and the shared weather-schedule builder. Physics, normal session/weather ticks and streaming/water authority promotion run in host order. Frozen retries retain simulation and presentation phase. Weather uses the existing versioned schedule; completed A4 payloads are file-acknowledged before completion publication. The existing TimeOfDaySweep family has an opt-in temporal capture leg. Native fixed-site capture remains native-pending. A4 unsupported-contributor refusal is preserved: ordinary spawn contributors and forward weather precipitation still prevent a complete sequence when active, pending fixed-site producer policy or missing producer coverage. Offline assembly selects version-1 sequence manifests through explicit --manifest PATH (build keyword manifest), accepts any filename inside or outside the frame directory, excludes the manifest from extras by file identity, requires complete status and the canonical plan hash, orders frames by the planned indices/ticks and verifies every payload size and SHA-256 through the same descriptors used for staging. Missing, extra, duplicate or invalid inputs refuse; invalid explicit manifests never fall back. Without the option the original legacy pipeline runs without discovery. Assembly caps input at 4096 frames, 12 payloads per frame, 128 MiB per payload and 512 MiB total; decoded RGB buffers reserve a separate 512 MiB with bounded dimensions. Requested MP4 requires ffmpeg; encoder failure preserves existing outputs and removes staged video. Registered stdlib-only regressions cover order, hashes, partial input, budgets, child-encoder failure and legacy byte parity. Offline advisory temporal measurements are recorded separately. No all-features runtime support is claimed. An explicit per-frame DeferredOnlyFixedSite renderer policy omits unsupported plants, decals, water, waterfalls, glass, foliage and particles only for admitted A4 diagnostic frames, and records deferred_only_fixed_site in capture render settings. The scene-compositing weather overlay and its snapshot are omitted; weather inputs to deferred lighting and sky remain. Scene-overlay grading, precipitation and all-features evidence are excluded. Water visibility evidence is invalidated at every frame start, including omitted submission and layer isolation. Paired replay refuses nonempty glass without prepared OIT targets, valid accumulation/resolve shaders or draw VAOs before changing capture state; ordinary glass rendering prepares resources, while resize retires the targets. Empty glass needs no OIT resources. Default rendering and unadmitted captures retain their refusals. Registered headless and Python source-contract regressions cover the reduced policy, active rain/snow/fog, water evidence lifetime and replay resource admission; native day/night and weather-cycle verification remain pending.
